gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Heavy, rounded and a bit like bent straw: that is Plakkaat up top. And Noto Sans Myanmar fills the line below with a dense, thick-looking strip of text and a broad, welcoming c that keeps a long passage easy to wade through.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-nabatae: Plakkaat draws its closed, heavy letters with the steadiness of a drawn string, every stroke curling back toward the stem. But Noto Sans Nabataean opens up below, its lowercase nearly cap-tall and its s curves wide, so a long stretch reads freely.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-nag-mun: Noto Sans Nag Mundari has curves that look half unwrapped. Plakkaat above it traces every stroke at the width of a single stylus, so the two sit together as bold rounded forms over a lowercase rivaling the capitals.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-nandina: Approachable is the mood of Noto Sans Nandinagari, with generous openings and short ascenders under a big lowercase body. But Plakkaat is best at closed, rounded-nib heavy letters, while the body font earns its place by staying open.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-newa: Noto Sans Newa reads with a clearly open mouth on the e and tall lowercase counters and bowls that let each word breathe. Plakkaat's closed, heavy forms make the contrast.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu reads tall, with a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke body, so lines feel lofty and spread out. Beside Plakkaat's hollow glass-tube lettering it feels light.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham leaves wide gaps in the e, and its tall lowercase bodies look bold in their own right. Noto Sans Ogham over a long stretch reads with a dense, open rhythm, a foil to Plakkaat's closed, heavy letters.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-ol-chik: Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds the tails of its curves well back, so words read as solid blocks rather than skylines. Plakkaat's rod-built letters earn their keep big and short.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-old-hun: Noto Sans Old Hungarian reads open, with large counters in the tall a, e and s. Even at tiny sizes those apertures stay clear, so under Plakkaat's flat, unswelling curves a long passage goes down easily.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-old-ita: Plakkaat squeezes its stroke like toothpaste in one steady line. Beside it, Noto Sans Old Italic sits with very little gap between x-height and cap height, and its curve endings kept well apart give the pair its strongest quality: smooth heft against open restraint.
